sources.title: Nintendo Defends Decision to Cut Mario and Yoshi Easter Eggs From The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
sources.text: Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Hidden away inside Hyrule Castle, the game's original 1998 version included a wall of portraits that featured Mario, Luigi, Peach, Bowser, and Yoshi artwork taken from Super Mario 64. Visit the same area in Nintendo's newly-launched Switch 2 version, however, and all references to the Mushroom Kingdom have been removed. On a similar note, a selection of Zelda: Twilight Princess artwork has also been cut, having been snuck in when Ocarina of Time was re-released on 3DS. Now, Nintendo has addressed its choice to remove these Easter eggs — and said that what was once a more "carefree" approach within Nintendo to referencing other games has been reconsidered. "Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal," legendary Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma told Game Informer . "Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing. "But looking at it now... given the overall way that we're creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time." While some fans might feel like it's a shame to see this more carefree attitude to Easter eggs is gone, it's fair to point out that Mario 64 Easter eggs (or Skyward Sword ones, for that matter) would make less sense today. Mario 64 was launched on the same platform as Ocarina of Time, of course, while Skyward Sword was released contemporaneously with the game's 3DS port. (Maybe Switch 2 just needs a new Mario game to actually arrive?) "I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game," Aonuma continued, "and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that... [But] you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way." "No hard feelings there," commented Skyward Sword director Hidemaro Fujibayashi, who returned as a producer for this remake. And one Mario reference does still survive via Talon — a character who is an obvious nod to Mario with his bushy moustache, plus red and blue overalls. Check out his necklace, and you'll see his golden Bowser charm remains intact, all these years later. Nintendo legend Shigeru Miyamoto has previously discussed the idea of the company's different franchises crossing over , and said that he wasn't a fan — except when it is Pikmin , which he wants to include wherever possible. Earlier today, Nintendo revealed that Ocarina of Time had already shifted 5.2 million copies and become the Switch 2's fastest-selling game so far. Meanwhile, players have been having fun in-game by performing everything from Linkin Park to the Titanic theme on ocarina . You can read our review of the game here , or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. sources.title: 10 Ways Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is Better Than the Original
sources.text: The original The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time has been certified as the highest-rated video game ever for a long time now. 2026’s Remake , however, has immediately climbed the charts and is currently this year’s top-rated title. The question then becomes, “Which one is actually better overall?” For my personal two cents, I still give the OG a slight edge. At the same time, that doesn’t take anything away from the Remake. In fact, 2026’s version of Ocarina is actually better in some cases. Let’s take a look at ten different ways Nintendo was able to take the classic and somehow improve on some aspects. Most obviously, the graphical and performance upgrades in OOT Remake are substantial. This isn’t a surprise at all since the OG is from the ’90s, but Remake still smashed it out of the park in terms of design and tone as well. Despite some concerns over glossy character models during the pre-launch phase of the game, the new art direction is constantly breathtaking and pulled off masterfully. Standouts are Lake Hylia with its gorgeous water effects, and Ganondorf’s Castle, which straight up looks like it’s ripped out of Mordor in Lord of the Rings. The hardest thing about going back for the original version of OOT is the control scheme and camera. Sure, the visuals are dated, but there’s a definite charm and style to them as well. The controls are just… old. This barrier to entry being removed in Zelda: Ocarina Remake was crucial to it succeeding in modern times. Thankfully, the right-stick camera works beautifully (though Z-Target centering was still kept in as well). Sword combat and shield blocking are fluid and snappy. Perhaps most importantly, however, is that projectile aiming can now be toggled between standard camera control and inverted. The 1998 game only offered inverted aiming, which is a total no-go for many modern gamers. There’s a certain charm in figuring out the auto-ledge jumping in N64 Ocarina, but it’s no surprise that having an actual, dedicated jump button in Remake is a massive improvement. Back in the day, Link’s jumping mechanics were the best Nintendo could muster, and we learned to adapt to them. But in 2026, not having an actual jump would’ve been a crime. This new ability also leads to some fun location and dungeon redesigns since Link can reach higher ledges and areas than ever before. A lot of players hopping into Remake (myself included) know almost everything about the N64 game. When picking up Remake, I wondered just how 1:1 everything would be, including things like gold skulltulas and room layouts. To my surprise, it was a blast to explore the new game and learn that many locations had been shuffled around or changed entirely. And this isn’t just a “better” change because it’s different. Instead, there are now several examples of things being placed more thoughtfully and satisfyingly in the game world. Take, for example, the Kokiri Sword, which now takes a little more parkour action to collect. I may know the lore and story of Zelda: Ocarina of Time better than any other video game. Upon recently replaying the OG, however, it’s funny how much of the narrative is a little bit underexplained. Case in point: the Triforce itself is shoddily explained, making it less impactful when considering why everyone seems to care so much about it. In Remake, most characters have a plethora of added or tweaked dialogue. A lot of this added exposition serves the game extremely well, making the stakes clearer and even giving us additional lore and info along the way. I didn’t expect to learn even more about Hyrule and the plot of the game in 2026, but the Remake gave me the opportunity. Growing up, we’d often have to make up video game character voices in our heads. Fully voice-acted games weren’t the norm yet. Aside from Navi shouting her classic “Hey!” and “Listen!” lines, the rest of the OG cast was relegated to grunts, screams, laughs, and moans. Hearing immediate narration voice-over when booting up Remake is a trip. For the most part, I found all the actor choices on-point, too. My personal standout is the English dub for Kaepora Gaebora, the Guiding Owl, played by Frank Todaro. There were doubts that Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s legendary soundtrack could be improved, but it somehow was. Of course, this is in large part due to the songs now being fully orchestrated, which was not an option on the Nintendo 64. Still, it wouldn’t have been hard to mess this one up with how beloved 1998’s tunes still are to this day. Thankfully, the full orchestration is gorgeous, as the new, sweeping melodies pack home way more emotion than ever before. Special shout-out to Saria’s Song, which comes back several times in a surprising, haunting fashion. While I wouldn’t say every dungeon was improved in the Remake, several were still fundamentally made better. In general, they’re all a bit more straightforward, which is nice for first-time players who aren’t used to retro game design. At the same time, simpler isn’t always better. In the case of dungeons like the Water Temple and Jabu-Jabu’s Belly, however, streamlining was the move. The migraine-inducing original Water Temple is reworked just enough that it went from my least favorite in the OG, to possibly my actual favorite in Remake. Most, if not all, of the dungeons are essentially at least on par with the original versions. The handful that actually made things better then stand out that much more this time around. While there aren’t too many challenging boss or enemy encounters in Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, fighting everything is still more fun than ever. This is thanks to many tweaks to encounter structure and entire enemy movesets. For example, King Dodongo now summons baby Dodongos during phases of the boss fight. Twinrova has an additional, arena-spanning spin attack. It’s a blast to have to reconsider and relearn these fights (and also practice them in the added Hall of Fallen Foes mode). sources.title: How to get the Goron Tunic in Zelda Ocarina of Time
sources.text: The Goron Tunic is a unique piece of equipment that allows Link to withstand high temperatures in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. If you try to explore the Death Mountain Crater without this item, Link's clothes will catch fire, and he will start losing health. While entering such a dangerous place might not sound like a good idea, you can't actually avoid it, as you'll need to traverse the area to reach the Fire Temple during the story. But don't fret. We've put this guide together to explain how to get the Goron Tunic in Zelda Ocarina of Time remake . After you turn into adult Link, you have two options when it comes to acquiring the Goron Tunic. You can either get it for free by talking to Link (the Goron Link!) in Goron City or buy it from the Shop Owner in Goron City for 600 rupees . Even if you have enough money, I would say that paying for the tunic is not a good option. To receive the tunic from Goron Link, you must find him in Goron City . You'll meet him as soon as you enter the city as adult Link. However, before you can talk to him, he will start rolling around the city's second layer. To stop him, you must hit them with a bomb . You can either use one of your own bombs or grab the bomb flowers that you find around the area. Once you finally hit Goron Link, talk to him and choose "The Fire Temple?" dialogue option to hear him explain what happened to Goron City. Next, select "I'll help you!" option, and Link will give you his Goron Tunic so you can help his father and the other Gorons who were taken to the Fire Temple. Just like the Zora Tunic , you activate the Goron Tunic's effect by equipping it in the Equipment menu. Although this tunic protects Link from the extreme temperatures inside Death Mountain Crater, it doesn't make Link immune to fire , so walking over the flames left by the volcanic rocks while wearing the Goron Tunic will still damage you. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is a little bit different than the original game, so if you need guides to help you through, we don’t blame you. We have walkthroughs for all the dungeons, from the Deku Tree to Ganondorf's Castle . We also have guides for the sillier, in-between parts of the game, like when you have to find Richard (the dog) or Cuccos . For those going for 100% completion, we also have guides on where to find every Piece of Heart , every Gold Skulltula token , and where to plant every Magic Bean .

sources.title: PlayStation cancels live-service shooter Fairgames
sources.text: Haven Games to "shift focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation" PlayStation has cancelled Fairgames, the live-service shooter previously in development at its Montreal-based subsidiary Haven Studios. In a statement to Bloomberg , PlayStation said Haven Studios will "shift focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." No jobs have been cut due to the cancellation. According to an email reviewed by Bloomberg, executives Sean Decker and John Doyle informed employees that a recent Fairgames playtest did not meet expectations. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," they said. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." Haven Studios' debut game was announced in 2023, initially scheduled for release last year, and later delayed to Spring 2026. Jade Raymond founded Haven Studios in 2021, and PlayStation Studios acquired the studio in 2022. Following Raymond's departure in May 2025 , executive producer Marie-Eve Danis and Pierre-François Sapinski were appointed co-studio heads. PlayStation started focusing on the live-service market in 2022 by acquiring Bungie for $3.6 billion . Former Sony Interactive Entertainment head Jim Ryan said the company aimed to launch more than ten live-service games by 2026 . Sony reduced the value of its acquisition by $765 million in the 2025/26 fiscal year after Destiny 2 and Marathon underperformed. Earlier this year, Bungie laid off 292 employees and ended development on Destiny 2. Following the game's final update, Bungie announced plans to reinstate vaulted campaigns , raids, and destinations to restore player trust. One of Sony’s most publicised live-service failures was Concord in 2024 , which was withdrawn from sale two weeks after release. Sony subsequently closed its developer Firewalk Studios , along with Neon Koi. Koi. In 2025, Sony cancelled two unannounced live service titles from Bend Studio and Bluepoint Games. The following year, Sony closed Bluepoint, resulting in 70 job losses . Sony Interactive CEO Hideaki Nishino previously said he wanted to "revitalise" live-service projects through a combination of first- and third-party content following its string of failures. "We believe that live service games are content that attracts users on a global level, so we want to continue to revitalise the market through both first-party and third-party content," Nishino said. "We are not only focusing on promoting new releases, but also considering what we can do with older titles in the medium to long term." He continued: "With live service games, it's important to continuously provide something. The genre itself is relatively new, and I think many people are trying various things, so we also want to continue to take on challenges within that context."

sources.text: Fairgames was revealed in 2023, but nothing more was ever seen of it. A Bloomberg report says Fairgames, a PvP heist shooter announced by Haven Studios and Sony in 2023 , has been cancelled. In something of a surprising twist, a PlayStation rep told the site there will be no layoffs as a result of the cancellation, as Haven will "shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." While it was announced three years ago, work on Fairgames appears to have started even further back, in 2021. Just a couple months after her high-profile split with Google Stadia , Assassin's Creed co-creator Jade Raymond announced the formation of Haven Studios , which was "working on an unannounced new IP for PlayStation." In 2022, right around the time former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan was talking about launching 12 live service games by 2025, Sony acquired the studio outright; a year after that, Fairplay was revealed to the world. But things have not gone smoothly since then. Helldivers 2 was a massive hit, but seven of those planned games were cancelled before release . Of the remaining games, one was Marathon , which endures but has not lived up to expectations, and another was Concord , one of the most famously disastrous game launches in years, which was taken offline less than two weeks after it launched, never to return. A live-service spinoff of the Horizon series, Hunters Gathering, was also reportedly rebooted after negative feedback from playtests . A partial accounting of canned multiplayer projects: The Concord catastrophe in particular seemed to shake Sony, which began reversing its live service strategy just a few months later. Fairgames itself looked to be in trouble in 2025 when Raymond departed Haven , reportedly after an external playtest left PlayStation leadership "concerned about how the game was received and its progress." The Bloomberg report says a more recent large-scale playtest produced similar results. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email sent to Haven Studios employees. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." The one bright spot to the cancellation is that no jobs will be cut because of it: A Sony rep told Bloomberg that Haven "will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." sources.title: PlayStation's embattled shooter Fairgames has finally been cancelled, a new report says, as live service push withers away
sources.text: After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames. The Haven-developed co-op heist shooter has been cancelled, with the silver lining that the studio is not closing down or laying off staff. According to a new Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest. Sony told staff on Tuesday of the playtest's poor reception and of its decision to end development. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PvP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." A PlayStation spokesperson later confirmed that developers at Haven will now support other teams within the PlayStation Studios group, as they continue to "explore new creative opportunities". Fairgames was initially announced in 2023 as one of several in-development live service games, as part of an initiative by former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan to create more than a dozen games that generate recurring revenue . Most of those titles were cancelled before they were even revealed, and those that made it out, such as Concord, flopped severely . Even Sony darling Guerrilla Games seemingly can't make it work, with recent reports saying the studio's Horizon Hunters Gathering - initially envisioned as a live service spin on the robo dinosaur series - will now shift into a more traditional co-op structure without live service elements. That's assuming the team can show a revamped version of the game to executives by December. The news of Fairgames' cancellation isn't surprising. The game has had a tumultuous development journey ever since its reveal. Initially set for release in 2025, the game was soon pushed back to 2026 , following the departure of studio founder Jade Raymond . Though Sony later reiterated its commitment to its remaining in-development live service titles , Fairgames was never shown to the public again. That same year, game director Daniel Drapeau left Haven - another key departure suggesting the game had difficulties and might not see release. Throughout that time, Fairgames has reportedly been reworked multiple times, with a plan for it to be re-revealed under a new name. That name is believed to be Break In, linked to a trademark Sony filed in May , but with the project cancelled, we may never know if that was the case.

Rockstar notes that Xbox Cloud Gaming will use the Xbox Series S graphics settings to stream to Xbox consoles. Xbox’s own announcement blog post only mentions Xbox Cloud Gaming streaming for Xbox Series X / S and Xbox One owners. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma says the cloud deal for Grand Theft Auto VI is “the first step in our new 10-year strategic partnership with Take-Two.” Sharma also says the game is “the most pre-ordered game ever on Microsoft Store.” Microsoft is also planning to add Grand Theft Auto V , Red Dead Redemption 2 , and more to Xbox Cloud Gaming in “the coming months.” What this all means is that Microsoft effectively has an exclusive on streaming Grand Theft Auto VI from the cloud for launch, albeit only to Xbox consoles. I originally reported last month that Microsoft had secured exclusive Grand Theft Auto VI cloud streaming rights, but Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball revealed on X that Microsoft wouldn’t be streaming Grand Theft Auto VI exclusively. While Microsoft’s contract might not specifically state exclusive, the end result is exclusive cloud gaming on Xbox, for now. Sony may well eventually announce its own cloud streaming plans for the game, but Rockstar Games notes that Grand Theft Auto VI “will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.” That’s not cloud streaming, though. I also initially reported that Grand Theft Auto VI would be available to stream on PC, simply because the entire point of Xbox Cloud Gaming is to make games available on Xbox consoles, TVs, PCs, and the web. It’s strange to see a rare exception for Grand Theft Auto VI , but not entirely surprising. Perhaps Microsoft will eventually be able to stream the PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI whenever it launches. Rockstar Games also confirms Grand Theft Auto VI will run at 30fps across PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S / X consoles. The main advantage of a PS5 Pro is ray-traced shadows and support for PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). Update, November 10th : Article updated with comments from Xbox.

sources.text: GTA 6 ganha novo teaser e inicia preload após recorde de pré-vendas Se você ainda não garantiu um console de nova geração só para jogar o game mais aguardado de todos os tempos, aqui vai uma boa e inesperada notícia: GTA 6 poderá ser jogado no Xbox One por meio do Xbox Cloud Gaming já no dia 19 de novembro , data de lançamento oficial da sequência. Segundo informações da própria Microsoft, GTA 6 é o título mais pré-encomendado de todos os tempos no Xbox Store, e a empresa recomenda que os jogadores iniciem a pré-instalação o quanto antes. A possibilidade é uma novidade importante, já que o console pertence à geração passada e não consegue executar o jogo nativamente. Nos consoles mais recentes da Microsoft, GTA 6 será executado diretamente no hardware. O Xbox Series X oferecerá a experiência nativa de console com melhor desempenho gráfico, enquanto o Series S será a opção mais acessível para jogar sem depender de streaming. Já no Xbox One, o funcionamento será diferente: o game será executado em servidores da Microsoft e transmitido pela internet por meio do Xbox Cloud Gaming. Nesse formato, o console não precisa processar o jogo, apenas reproduzir a transmissão. Segundo a Microsoft, a versão transmitida pela nuvem utilizará as configurações gráficas do Xbox Series S — e, assim como em todos os consoles, também rodará a 30 FPS . Além disso, a empresa confirmou que jogadores de mercados compatíveis poderão comprar tempo de jogo na nuvem a partir de 11 de novembro, sem precisar de uma assinatura do Game Pass. Vale lembrar que o jogo precisa ser adquirido separadamente para acessar a transmissão . Apesar de GTA 6 chegar ao Xbox One por streaming, o jogo infelizmente não poderá ser executado no PS4 . O console da Sony não receberá uma versão nativa do título, e a Rockstar não anunciou suporte ao jogo por meio de serviços de nuvem da PlayStation. A diferença está justamente na forma de funcionamento do Xbox Cloud Gaming. A PlayStation também oferece streaming de jogos em nuvem por meio dos planos mais completos do PS Plus Premium, mas a disponibilidade varia de acordo com a região e o catálogo de títulos compatíveis. Até o momento, não há confirmação de que GTA 6 será oferecido dessa maneira no serviço. Portanto, entre os consoles da geração passada, apenas o Xbox One terá acesso a GTA 6 por meio de streaming na nuvem. No caso do PS4, os jogadores não poderão aproveitar o lançamento, já que não existe uma versão compatível anunciada para o aparelho. Lembrando que GTA 6 será lançado em 19 de novembro de 2026 para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S. O título será disponibilizado exclusivamente nos consoles de atual geração inicialmente — mas é bastante provável que uma versão de PC também chegue no primeiro trimestre de 2027, segundo fortes rumores que circularam recentemente . sources.text: Grand Theft Auto V is the reigning game of all time. One of gamingâs most undeniable cultural exports. An ugly game that casts one unbelievable shadow. A title so massive, itâs become damn near impossible to recreate without burning down your development studio in 2026. Revisiting it in the lead-up to GTA VI âs release later this year has been illuminating in many ways, but the thing Iâm perhaps most struck by about the 2013 hit is how miserable it is. What a fascinating thing to exist in the supposed upper echelon of the gaming pantheon. GTA V is filled with all kinds of missions and objectivesâthe stuff that modern gaming parlance constantly calls “content.” Really, it turns everything into content for you to check off. It’s got big missions and small ones. Simple, boring ones that occasionally lull you to sleep. Distractions like tennis and drag racing. And, on the other end, massive, multi-part setpieces that get the blood pumping a little more efficiently. A gulf separates these sequences. Sometimes I’m little more than a glorified cabbie, at other times a glorified avatar of the âAmerican dreamââa ball of boredom, rage, and discontent at The Way Things Are, armed with a rifle aimed at nothing in particular. Lots of it feels utterly meaningless. Stealing the occasional getaway vehicle and quietly parking it in a nearby lot often counts as a mission, one I hate after doing it multiple times in my ~50 hours revisiting GTA V . Not that its more pulse-pounding action is especially noteworthy either. The game’s crosshair, for example, is wholly unremarkable. It’s just a dot. A dot that, by default, magnetizes to the often nameless nobodies on the other end of your barrel, as if to smooth any friction that could possibly arise in the instant between when you see a foe and when you pull the trigger on your weapon of choice.Â Many other shooters feature different crosshairs depending on the weapon. A grenade launcher might suggest an arc. A sniper rifle, too. A shotgun blast has a wider spread, and a crosshair usually indicates its range. But time and time again, GTA V plays it cool, calm, and detached with its minimalist crosshair. It doesn’t want to bore you with calculating distances and trajectories. It wants you to endlessly put holes in cops, gangsters, hillbillies, rival drug enterprises, federal agents, clowns, aliens, and everything in between, while occasionally piloting several classes of vehicle in increasingly linear scenarios. It doesn’t feel wholly good or bad; it feels likeâ¦nothing.Â Driving around the state of San Andreas and shooting things feels like nothing . A kind of nothing that quicklyâ easily âfills dozens of hours. Like a chore. Maybe that’s the best way to describe GTA V . Well, if itâs going to be such a chore, it feels, at least, like GTA V should aim that tedium at some larger point, shouldn’t it? It kind of does. Each of its endeavors, be it a mundane task, an odd job to rustle up some cash, or a riotous heist spilled out on the streets of not-LA, does in fact feel pointed. Compulsive, even. At least in part because they feel like the backdrop for the gameâs occasionally devastating musings that hit with the force of, well, a getaway vehicle.Â The most consequential series of missions among GTA V ‘s errands is largely divorced from the thrust of its campaign. Itâs got nothing to do with heists and has nothing to do with two-thirds of the gameâs playable trio. Itâs got nothing to do with the city of Los Santos, even. Far up in the middle of Nowhere, Blaine County, is an unsavory duo called the Minute Men, who are on a collision course with a similarly ugly force by the name of Trevor Phillipsâa walking, talking (usually swearing) cancer and truly one of the most detestable protagonists a game has ever saddled a player with.Â The Minute Menâs contributions to GTA V are small but important. Over a triptych of morally repugnant descents into darkness that only Trevor can take on, they try to prove the righteousness of their cause. In a move that felt like a cavity opening in my soul, Trevor rides along with Joe and Josef, two members of the âCivil Border Patrol,â as they chase down and detain Mexican-American citizens across the countryside. Or as one of them says, in his native Russian on American soil, âWell-motivated people, eager to do low-level jobs at any wage to support their families.âÂ These missions are, like the rest of GTA V âs offerings, pretty unremarkable in their construction. You chase after these poor souls in a patrol vehicleâa park rangerâs van with hardly a new splash of paintâtase them (another drab crosshair) and eventually escort them back to the vehicle, where they are subsequently driven to a somewhat ambiguous fate. The whole thing would only run about 15 minutes if the missions were stitched together, and ends with little fanfare. All in all, these excursions with the Civil Border Patrol are a perfect microcosm of what GTA V actually excels at: being a banal cascade of senseless violence and bigotry, bookended by a smug but empty wink. A shockingly vivid reflection of our depravity and our inability to break from it. A post-modern vision of what passes for a video game and what can be fun about it.Â Many of GTA V âs most memorable moments echo this particular sensibility, as has become customary of the franchise, which has satirized America and its long-running series of systemic failures over the past 25 years. The mission “Friend Request,” which involves another of the gameâs protagonists, named Michael, breaking into the headquarters of a Facebook analog called Life Invader, is a perfect example. In it Michael, and thus the player, live out what has become, in the years since the gameâs release, an even more entertaining fantasy, making a very public example of a tech mogul with an inflated ego and a penchant for flagrant violations of child labor laws. sources.text: Both platforms encourage players to pre-load the game to minimise potential delays and crashes on launch day Grand Theft Auto 6 has become the most pre-ordered game on the PlayStation Store and Microsoft Store. Sensor Tower's GTA 6 sales tracker currently estimates nearly 9.69 million pre-orders worldwide, generating $942 million in revenue. These figures have risen significantly in one week. On November 7, the tracker reported nearly eight million pre-orders and $751 million in revenue. GTA 6 pre-orders have exceeded expectations for Rockstar's parent company Take-Two Interactive . "[We cannot] disclose the numbers, but the point that we're making is our prior expectations obviously were aligned with our guidance, and the pre-orders are far exceeding our original expectations," Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick recently told GamesIndustry.biz . "We're maintaining our guidance, because the release is only 10 days away and we'll know a lot more after the release." In Take-Two's recent Q2 results , Zelnick said the company expects to "deliver a historic year" as a result of GTA 6's launch. Since November 10, GTA 6 has been available to pre-load on PlayStation and Xbox. Both platforms recommend pre-loading to help prevent crashes and delays on launch day, much like what happened with Hollow Knight: Silksong last year . GamesIndustry.biz recently consulted experts on whether GTA 6 could overwhelm internet traffic and if pre-loading will help manage download demand before next week's release. GamesDiscoverCo newsletter author Simon Carless said that "having an extra nine days to gradually send out the bulk of the data to players' computers is vital. There still might be a Day 1 patch/extra download, but if so, it'll be very incremental." Investor and strategic advisor Joost van Dreunen suggested the download bottleneck could still come on launch day, when "tens of millions day-of buyers, not a few hundred thousand" will be downloading the game.

sources.text: On PC, however, GTA 6 remains among the least pre-ordered games of all time because, well, you know. It goes without saying (yet here I am saying it) that Grand Theft Auto 6 is going to be huge. We don't really have a sense as to just how huge at this point: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has boasted that GTA 6 preorder numbers are " unprecedented ," but he's refused to provide specifics because "the raw numbers could be potentially misleading." But huge, for sure. Now both Sony and Xbox have joined in the 'gonna be huge' chorus, each of them announcing that preorders for GTA 6 are, definitionally, unprecedented . "Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store," Sony proclaimed on the PlayStation Blog . "Given this unprecedented demand, we’ve joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they’re ready to play on launch day. We’ve also adopted a rolling midnight launch by country, beginning at 12:00AM NZDT in New Zealand and running across the globe as respective countries hit midnight on November 19." Xbox made a similar announcement on its own website, calling GTA 6 "the most pre-ordered title of all time on the Microsoft Store" and encouraging users to begin preloading as soon as possible because of "the unprecedented demand" for the game. Alongside Xbox Series X/S consoles, Xbox said GTA 6 will also be playable on Xbox One consoles through Xbox Cloud Gaming. That service is also available on PC, but Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Bell confirmed in October that GTA 6 will not be streamable on our platform . But while nobody is serving up specifics on the number of GTA 6 copies sold via preorder, we do have a rough indicator of how much money Take-Two expects to make when it comes out of the gate. The publisher is projecting net bookings of $3.35 to $3.5 billion for its current fiscal quarter, "driven by the groundbreaking release of Grand Theft Auto 6" on November 19. That's roughly double what Take-Two took in during the same quarter in its previous year, when it reported net bookings of $1.76 billion. "The launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 is ten days away and, with pre-orders continuing to reach unprecedented levels, we expect to deliver an historic year for our company," Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said during yesterday's quarterly financial report. sources.text: GTA 6 ganha novo teaser e inicia preload após recorde de pré-vendas A poucos dias da estreia de GTA 6 , a Sony acaba de anunciar que o PlayStation 5 ultrapassou oficialmente a marca de 100 milhões de unidades vendidas. O resultado pode ter sido impulsionado pela expectativa em torno do novo jogo da Rockstar, que chega ao mercado em novembro — embora isso seja mera especulação da nossa parte. Segundo os dados divulgados pela empresa, o console atingiu o marco em 10 de novembro. Isso significa que pelo menos 2,1 milhões de unidades foram enviadas desde 30 de setembro, quando a Sony havia informado que o PS5 acumulava 97,9 milhões de consoles vendidos . Lançado em novembro de 2020, o PlayStation 5 precisou de quase seis anos para ultrapassar a marca de 100 milhões de unidades vendidas. O resultado é semelhante ao registrado pelo PlayStation 4, que atingiu o mesmo número em junho de 2019 — cerca de cinco anos e sete meses após sua estreia. Com isso, o PS5 entra para um grupo restrito de consoles que ultrapassaram a marca de 100 milhões de unidades comercializadas. Até o momento, apenas sete videogames alcançaram esse resultado, todos fabricados pela Nintendo ou pela Sony. Confira a lista: Apesar de ter alcançado um número expressivo, o ritmo de vendas do PS5 vem diminuindo gradualmente, como costuma acontecer com consoles que chegam ao sexto ano de mercado — mas isso pode mudar com a chegada iminente de GTA 6 . A proximidade do lançamento de GTA 6 pode ter contribuído para o aumento recente na procura pelo PlayStation 5. Como o novo jogo da Rockstar é um dos lançamentos mais aguardados da indústria, parte do público pode estar aproveitando o período para comprar o console antes da estreia. Embora a Sony não tenha confirmado uma relação direta entre o desempenho comercial do PS5 e a chegada do game, o aumento de pelo menos 2,1 milhões de unidades enviadas desde o fim de setembro coincide com a reta final da campanha de lançamento. Outro fator que pode influenciar as vendas é a expectativa de que GTA 6 seja um dos principais jogos da geração atual. Como o título chegará ao PS5 e ao Xbox Series X|S, consumidores que ainda não possuem um dos consoles podem decidir fazer a compra para jogar a novidade. Enquanto o PS5 continua vendendo, o sucessor do console ainda pode demorar alguns anos para chegar ao mercado. No início deste ano, David Gibson, analista sênior da MST Financial, publicou um relatório indicando que o ciclo de vida do aparelho atual deve ser mais longo do que algumas previsões anteriores sugeriam. “A Sony espera que o ciclo de vida do PS5 seja prolongado, e o lançamento do PS6 provavelmente será adiado por mais tempo do que muitos esperavam”, afirmou Gibson em sua análise. A possibilidade de um lançamento mais distante também foi reforçada pelo CEO da Sony, Hiroki Totoki. Durante teleconferência sobre os resultados financeiros mais recentes da companhia, o executivo afirmou que a empresa ainda não havia definido uma data para a chegada do PlayStation 6. Mesmo sem uma previsão oficial, alguns analistas trabalham com a possibilidade de que o novo videogame seja lançado em meados de 2028. A avaliação de Gibson, no entanto, aponta que o sucessor do PS5 pode chegar ainda mais tarde do previsto por conta da crise de chips que encareceu consideravelmente componentes de hardware. sources.text: Rockstar Games has today clarified a few remaining details about Grand Theft Auto 6's framerate target and visual settings on PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X/S . And as part of the same announcement , the developer revealed a key detail about the game's cloud streaming options. GTA 6 will be available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming. However, this is only possible on Xbox Series X/S consoles, as well as - surprisingly - the last generation console, Xbox One. Notably, that means you can't use Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream to PC, or other devices, despite it being useable there. You may recall that in early October, a Verge report said Microsoft had acquired exclusive cloud streaming rights for GTA 6, with the understanding being that the game would be available to stream on any XCloud-supported device - as in, to PC as well. Considering the loss in quality inherent in cloud streaming, this will make for a less-than-ideal way of experiencing the game. Beyond cloud streaming, GTA 6 supports Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox, so you can stream the game on your local network to any device, from a PS5 or Xbox Series X/S console. sources.title: Side Effects Guaranteed in the First DLC For The Outer Worlds 2, Coming December 2
sources.text: A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the ship’s crew in suspended animation. All signs point to foul play, especially the puddle of what was most likely a person. You recover a video message left by the captain of the vessel, who explains that the crew has been contaminated with something while on a heist that will cause explosive cell death unless they find a cure. And by explosive cell death, she means more like a… “liquefaction”. By the looks of the puddle on the floor: liquefaction indeed. The stakes are set for the release of the first of a two-part narrative DLC expansion of The Outer Worlds 2 on December 2. In Side Effects Guaranteed , the video message you found leads you to Gordon Hazen, one of the leading agents in Sub Rosa, a criminal organization made up of like-minded individuals who have chosen to live their lives stealing from the various factions instead of working for them. Gordon in turn sends you to Elysium Valley, a new region on Eden that is home to a settlement of former Protectorate subjects that have been forgotten by their Protectorate leaders. He believes they may have the answers to saving his crew. He personally favors diplomacy over violence but needs you to do whatever you need to in order to get the information he needs. But Gordon isn’t the only one with interest in Elysium Valley. Another Sub Rosa agent, Algernon Lankester, wants to recruit you to help him exploit the subjects for his own personal gain. The fate of the subjects, the frozen Sub Rosa agents, and the future of Sub Rosa itself is up for you, our intrepid Commander, to decide. A new narrative story is not all that will be coming when Side Effects Guaranteed launches in a few weeks, however. Along with the new region of Elysium Valley to explore, players will encounter new threats like vicious canids and primal sprats. What’s a primal sprat? Just a normal sprat, but about 100 times the size. Surely, they’re just as friendly and forgiving of all the time you “accidentally” shot their much smaller cousins while exploring Arcadia. With these new threats comes the ability to make your Commander even stronger and, of course, more flawed (but in a good way). The level cap will increase from 30 to 36, bringing more skill points to broaden your build. Being able to go to level 36 also means there are three more perks you can acquire, with 15 brand new perks being added into the mix. Four new flaws will also be introduced that can change how your Commander plays, like “Lethally Tolerant,” a flaw that recognizes your built-up resistance to chemicals so your max toxicity will increase. This is great in the moment, but if you ever experience a Toxicity Crash, you will die instantly. Another example is “Must Have Been the Wind,” which will mark an “assassination target” for a combat group. Killing the target will grant a 20% damage and speed buff until the combat ends, but failing to do so or attacking someone who isn’t the target applies a 10% damage and speed debuff to the player for 30 seconds. Truly rewards that come with great risks. Side Effects Guaranteed will also see new weapons, new armors, and new outfits for each of the companions, as well as a brand-new Sub Rosa-run radio station featuring 20 new songs for the game. For those who want to jump straight to the action in the DLC, a new alternate starting point is being added to the main menu when you choose a new game that will allow you to start with a custom save that lands you at the start of the DLC. Start the game, allot your skill and perk points, and enjoy Side Effects Guaranteed right away! This jam-packed adventure with a deep story and systems to build your ideal commander will set up the next DLC for The Outer Worlds 2 that will be coming in Spring of 2027, and choices made will directly impact the next DLC. Part one of this overarching expansion story, Side Effects Guaranteed , will release on December 2 for $14.99, or is available in the Premium Edition or Premium Edition Upgrade for The Outer Worlds 2 .

stories.title: Tekken Legend Katsuhiro Harada Says He Wishes 'Hardware Like the Xbox Series S Wouldn't Be Released'
stories.summary: Tekken development legend Katsuhiro Harada had some strong comments for Microsoft's lower-powered Xbox Series S console, dubbing it a "weaker child" with "awkwardly lower performance."

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Tekken Legend Katsuhiro Harada Says He Wishes 'Hardware Like the Xbox Series S Wouldn't Be Released'
sources.text: Tekken development legend Katsuhiro Harada had some strong comments for Microsoft's lower-powered Xbox Series S console, dubbing it a "weaker child" with "awkwardly lower performance." A number of video game developers have struggled with the Xbox Series S while following Microsoft's feature parity rules across Xbox Series consoles. Baldur's Gate 3 famously came to Xbox a few months late and required the help of Microsoft's engineers to get the game's split-screen co-op working on Series S . More recently, the developer of breakout shooter Wardogs admitted that the limitations of the Xbox Series S had stopped it from adding certain things to the game . Indeed, one of the questions facing Microsoft ever since the release of the Xbox Series S back in 2020 is whether it would be willing to allow developers and publishers to release a game on Xbox Series X only, leaving Xbox Series S behind. As it stands, Xbox mandates that video games launch on both or none at all, and that there should be main feature parity between each version. In a roundtable discussion held at the Console Game Developers Conference in Korea, Harada slammed the Series S and attempted to encourage Cyberpunk 2077 associate game director Paweł Sasko to join in the pile-on, too. "There's something I really want to say while I have the floor," Harada began (thanks, Inven Global ), "since a senior Xbox official is actually in attendance here today, I wish hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released (laughs)." Throughout his years in charge of Tekken, Harada has become known as a colorful character happy to express his opinions freely. And, to be fair, it sounds like Harada made the comment knowing he was being rather cheeky. But the developer then continued to explain his position further — and have Sasko back him up, following reports that CD Projekt struggled with Cyberpunk 2077's Series S version. "I want to ask director Paweł personally," Harada continued. "Honestly, weren't you upset inside because of Series S?" "It constantly throws challenges at us and forces us to optimize our code very cleanly," Sasko responded, appearing to tiptoe around the subject. "You just used a very polite and elegant way to say 'Xbox Series S sucks,' right?" Harada ploughed on. "Low memory is an issue, but the hardest part is that it's a device so similar to Series X while having awkwardly lower performance. When porting to Switch 2, developers can shift their mindset to 'Switch 2 is a distinct device for Nintendo fans!' But with Xbox, after delivering your absolute best output, it feels like having to do extra work for a slightly weaker child." Gosh. Tell us what you really think, Harada! "Furthermore," he continued further, "in markets like the U.S., there are more Series S users than Series X users, so we can't just cut corners. Yet after launch, Series S users direct their complaints at us developers rather than Microsoft, asking 'Why is texture resolution lower only on Series S?'" While Harada's comments will likely not come as a shock to many developers who have been tasked with releasing games across the Xbox Series family this generation, it is rare to hear someone of Harada's prominence discussing the Series S' drawbacks out loud. In response — and in a continued attempt to not say anything that would get him in trouble — Sasko acknowledged that such Series S drawbacks were real, but that the console also offered a lot of positives. Its more affordable price point meant that developers could get their games played by a wider audience, Sasko offered, while opimtization breakthroughs initially made for Series S had also benefited Cyberpunk 2077 across all platforms. Acknowledging Sasko's more positive take, Harada concluded that he was now worried Microsoft would "feel reassured and release a successor like 'Helix S' for the next-gen Xbox as well (laughs)." Will Xbox release a lower-powered Helix console? It's unclear. After earlier reports that suggested the new console was reportedly targeting a holiday 2027 launch , more recent estimates have pointed to a 2028 launch for the machine — at an eyewatering $1,200 - $1,800 price point . Maybe that will make Harada reconsider? Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

Yet after launch, Series S users direct their complaints at us developers rather than Microsoft , asking ‘why is texture resolution lower only on Series S?'” Sasko added that he agreed with Harada’s take, but added that being forced to optimise for systems like Xbox Series S can be beneficial for performance on higher spec systems. “Harada speaks a lot of truth,” he explained. “Players don’t fully understand the technical context behind why fewer characters appear on screen or why visuals are downgraded. “However, intensely optimizing for lower-spec platforms definitely brings the benefit of making the game run significantly better across all platforms, including PS5 , high-end PCs, and handhelds like Steam Deck and ROG Ally. “Recently, with Cyberpunk 2077 Version 2.5, we applied optimization breakthroughs gained while preparing the Switch 2 launch title (which involved a team of 80 to 100 people for over a year) back to all other platforms with great effect. “And the biggest advantage of Series S is that its affordable price makes it accessible. Not every gamer can buy expensive high-end hardware, so from a developer’s perspective, even if the strict constraints are painful, there is a silver lining in expanding market penetration to deliver the game to more players.” Harada joked that the Xbox member in the audience appeared to like what Sasko was saying, and that he was concerned he would come to the conclusion that the Series S was being praised. “Director PaweÅ packaged Series S so gracefully that the Microsoft representative in the audience keeps nodding along,” he said. “I’m worried they’ll feel reassured and release a successor like ‘Helix S’ for the next-gen Xbox as well.”

stories.title: Under pressure, Big Walk studio reveals it used generative AI "sparingly" while making its hit 2026 game
stories.summary: Australian developer House House has revealed it used generative AI "sparingly" to help make celebrated, indie, multiplayer puzzle game Big Walk. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Under pressure, Big Walk studio reveals it used generative AI "sparingly" while making its hit 2026 game
sources.text: "It has become a matter of public interest." Australian developer House House has revealed it used generative AI "sparingly" to help make celebrated, indie, multiplayer puzzle game Big Walk. In a statement sent to Aftermath - following a judging fallout related to the Independent Games Festival - House House revealed it had used large language models primarily to help debug the game's code. "In the final stretch of Big Walk's development, LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs," the developer said. "In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code - we'd estimate that well under 0.1 percent of Big Walk's code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game." House House added: "The primary use case for House House's use of LLMs was to research, via chatbots, issues we encountered with third-party code." The studio's revelation comes after a sizeable number of IGF jurors - 19 of them - issued a statement saying they would not vote for any game that used generative AI during its development. This was done after seeing "a significant increase" in entry submissions involving generative AI use, which "set off some fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools". And rather than not vote for these in silence, a collection of jurors decided to take a public stand. House House hadn't disclosed Big Walk generative AI use anywhere before disclosing it for its IGF submission. "We have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage," the studio explained. "We are posting this disclosure as it has become a matter of public interest." House House added: "This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal. We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as 'inevitable'. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to video games and our world, and apologise that Big Walk's LLM usage may not meet their standards. "Big Walk was developed without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards." It's a revelation that's likely to leave a taint of some degree on one of this year's brightest stars - a game Eurogamer awarded a full five stars to in its Big Walk review .

Some Independent Games Festival (IGF) jurors published a statement yesterday saying they would not vote for games that use generative AI in “any capacity.” Soon after, the developer of indie hit Big Walk has published a statement saying it “sparingly” used AI in the “final stretch” of the game’s development to “help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs.” According to the jurors’ statement , a copy of which was posted by Austin Walker, while this year’s IGF entries have been “incredible,” there has been “a significant increase” in the number of games “developed with generative AI tools,” leading to “fairly intense discussion and disagreement” with no “universal consensus.” The statement includes a list of beliefs, including that generative AI has “negative effects,” that AI-generated code is “not an exception to these harms,” and that use of AI tools is “not a forgone conclusion in our industry.” IGF jurors that signed include Telling Lies and Immortality creator Sam Barlow and Celeste composer Lena Raine . The jurors say that the statement doesn’t speak for IGF as an organization or for all IGF jury members, noting that some voiced concern about being able to safely sign “without professional blowback.” One contentious title was apparently Big Walk , the co-op adventure game from Untitled Goose Game developer House House. House House noted it turned to the “LLM chatbot” after researching the problem “extensively” and even speaking to an engineer at Unity. The studio said it disclosed its AI usage as part of its IGF submission, though it has not disclosed AI usage on Big Walk ’s Steam page because “the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage.” “This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal,” House House said. “We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as ‘inevitable’. sources.text: If you're a World of Warcraft: Forever player you're almost certainly having your free time drained as you chain yourself to your desktop PC to play the game, or maybe a laptop. But for a small selection of true enthusiasts, the game is already working on mobile and handheld devices. One such person showing off WoW: Forever on the go is none other than director of publishing at Larian, Michael Douse, who took to Twitter to show off the MMO being played on an AYN Thor device. For those who don't know, this is a fancy android handheld console, a sort of beefed up DS for the modern handheld aficionado. "Arguably too many layers of abstraction," writes Douse. In the picture he posted, you can see the player character viewable on the Thor's top screen, while the map, text chat, skill UI, and buffs viewable on the bottom. It looks pretty cool, and is made possible due to JReese702's Github mod you can download at your leisure. Arguably too many layers of abstraction pic.twitter.com/VjW0IX00Gg But it's not the only mo-bell at the ball. Another Github WoW: Forever mod, WolkaraForever , gets the game playable on the iPhone Duo. As highlighted by CEO of esports company 100 Thieves Alex Wechsler on Twitter , the game looks to be ported pretty well to the phone, with mobile touchscreen controls viewable on both sides of the screen. Be warned though, as confirmed by Wechsler in a Twitter reply, it'll get your phone running hot . As a father of 2 kids and always having wanted to play WOW, I’ve finally found a way 🥹 pic.twitter.com/eIVn0gn1WC This coming alongside World of Warcraft: Forever's built-in (and very good) controller support could mean the game has real potential to spread far and wide across the vast array of different hardware out there. Blizzard has already hinted at plans of porting the game to other platforms , so who knows? Maybe we can expect an official mobile port to tread the path paved by these community-made mods.

sources.title: Blizzard knows World of Warcraft: Forever has a gold problem
sources.text: Developers are turning to buffs over the old XP-to-gold conversion mechanic Blizzard is meeting gold-starved World of Warcraft: Forever players halfway by making more quests more generous regarding the resource. That said, an old feature that plenty used to grind gold is staying gone. When WoW: Forever launched, players racing to level up as swiftly as possible found that the XP-to-gold conversion for quests completed at max level was no longer present. If you'd like a quick history lesson, Blizzard added the feature to OG WoW before Burning Crusade launched, and it worked simply – once you're at max level, you get gold instead of XP. The decision not to include that feature in World of Warcraft: Forever hasn't been popular. As such, Blizzard has made an appearance online to explain some of its rationale. "We left that functionality in place in Classic Era in 2019, but we decided that for WoW: Forever, we would remove the XP-to-Gold conversion, as it created an incentive for players to hold a full quest log worth of completed quests to hand in after hitting level 60 for maximum gold returns," community lead Randy "Kaivax" Jordan explains in a forum post . "Under those conditions, the optimal way for players to level to 60 was to simply grind creatures for XP and not hand in quests at all, which is not a design we want to retain in WoW: Forever." Jordan continues by explaining that one thing Blizzard did not account for, however, is that only 25% quests in the original World of Warcraft actually provide raw gold rewards. So on that front, Blizzard is saying, yeah, actually you might have a point if you think the MMO is being stingy. But hopefully not any longer. Blizzard has now released a World of Warcraft: Forever patch that ensures most quests at level 48 and above now additionally reward gold. That said, don't expect the return of XP-to-gold conversion, as "it would be inappropriate" to have players keep hold of quests rather than hand them in. "This change brings high-level quests in line with the rest of questing in WoW: Forever, with the goal of giving players a good reason to complete those quests while leveling up to 60 and thereafter," Blizzard explains in a new patch post . "Quests that were not affected by this change include those that already reward valuable items, repeatable quests, and those that don't provide significant rewards because they're quick, easy, or trivial to complete." sources.title: Bandai Namco closes Reflector Entertainment, expects to post €21m loss in Q3 as a result
sources.text: Unknown 9 developer was acquired by Bandai Namco in 2020 Bandai Namco is closing Unknown 9: Awakening developer Reflector Entertainment. In a press briefing , Bandai Namco stated that "after comprehensively considering future business plans, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation," it has decided to dissolve and liquidate Reflector. The publisher expects to "post an extraordinary loss of approximately €21 million" for Reflector in its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. Bandai Namco acquired Montreal-based Reflector in 2020 for an undisclosed sum. It also acquired the studio's subsidiary, Reflector Interactive Productions. Reflector was founded in 2016 by Alexandre Amancio and Lune Rouge. Reflector is known for the 2024 action-adventure title Unknown 9: Awakening. It was created as a transmedia franchise, including a podcast audio drama, novels, and a comic book series. A month after launch, the studio announced it had cut 18% of its workforce . The studio attributed the layoffs to a new development phase, stating that affected employees weren't assigned to roles its active projects needed at the time. Further redundancies occurred in 2025 after the decision "not to greenlight" an unannounced project. The studio also cancelled the Unknown 9 franchise due to low sales . Reflector CEO Hervé Hoerdt acknowledged that Unknown 9 did not meet expectations "despite numerous timeline adjustments and investments." "This decision correlates directly with the failure of the studio's ambitious and courageous first project, a new IP with a rich transmedia universe."

Marathon ‘s Symbiosis update arrives December 8, bringing new PvE and PvP modes, weapons, a Runner shell, and expanded areas to explore on Tau Ceti IV. Today we’ve got first details on the updated Perimeter zone, Expedition mode, and more. Updated Perimeter zone: Fungal growth and alien life have transformed Perimeter, introducing new playable spaces including the underground Burrows and submerged Reservoir. Runners will also encounter the Tick Queen, who lurks deep beneath the surface. Expedition: Phase 1 of a new PvE-only mode built around a three-run series. Play solo or with a crew, face new combat and environmental challenges without PvP threats, and use Flash Boosts to shape your build during a run. Deathmatch (Beta): An experimental PvP mode featuring bite-sized 3v3 Team Deathmatch matches. Two crews compete for points without risking their permanent loadouts. Limbo: A new social space where Runners can connect, test weapons and gear in firing ranges, and challenge each other in a dueling pit. Bishop Runner shell: A new Runner shell built around the fantasy of a fast, surgical blade-wielding robot. New weapons: The V17 Flamethrower brings short-range area denial, while the Maverick introduces a new revolver archetype with a hand-cannon feel. sources.text: First-person psychological horror game Don’t Fret will launch for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , and PC via Steam and Microsoft Store on December 8, publisher Digital Pajamas and developer Scary Kid Studios announced. Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page : Don’t Fret is a first person psychological mascot-horror puzzle game, where music and horror intertwine in ways never before seen by the indie gaming community. Navigate the hallways of Harmonic Heights as “Fret,” a young talented guitar who is in search of finding a way back home. Meet Fret, a sentient guitar trapped in a nightmare of music and madness. Navigate the decaying halls of Harmonic Heights, uncover its secrets, and confront the horrors in a music world. Step into the visually stunning world of Don’t Fret , where every instrument, hallway, and shadow is alive with purpose. The game’s bold art direction blends psychological horror with musical surrealism, creating an unforgettable atmosphere that sets it apart from every other indie horror title. Shattering the boundaries of traditional indie horror with an expansive world spanning dozens of handcrafted environments—from classrooms and underground tunnels, to outside courtyards, gondola rides, and more. Armação de Corredor “Bishop”: uma nova armação inspirada na ideia de um robô veloz com lâminas e ataques precisos e letais. Novas armas: o Lança-Chamas V17 possibilita o controle de área em curto alcance, enquanto o Maverick surge com um novo arquétipo de revólveres com a pegada “canhão de mão”. Todos poderão curtir Marathon durante a Semana de Jogo Aberto, de 8 a 15 de dezembro, junto do lançamento de Simbiose. Marathon está disponível agora mesmo no PS5 , com integração entre plataformas e suporte a salvamento integrado entre plataformas. A atualização Simbiose sai em 8 de dezembro para todos os jogadores. *Jogar requer acesso à internet e uma assinatura paga no console (vendida separadamente). **Salvamento entre plataformas requer uma conexão com a internet, e, para cada sistema em que você jogar: 1) uma cópia do jogo Marathon compatível com o sistema (outras versões vendidas separadamente); e 2) uma conta da rede do sistema vinculada à sua conta da Bungie.net.
